attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both parts: losses every quarter now, and company projections that profit is years away. 'Won't make a profit' describes what the projections said at the time, not a new forecast.

contract.note: Reading 'losing money' as company-wide net loss, checked against the latest full quarter before the post, is a fair and ordinary reading. The result depends on the accounting basis, which the speaker never named.

evidence.note: WSJ reports company documents projecting profit in 2030. That fits the projection clause, but the documents date from summer 2025 and the profit measure isn't defined. It says nothing about quarterly results.
Reports an annual 2025 operating loss of about $21B. It is annual and operating, not quarterly net, so it cannot show a loss in every quarter.
The CFO's remark that OpenAI could break even is a hypothetical about a different strategy, not actual profit. Cash-flow positive projected for 2029-30 is a different measure.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no quarterly net results through Q4 2025, so 'losing money every quarter' can't be checked. The evidence leans toward the projection clause (profit around 2030), but it doesn't show the projection that was current on Feb 13, 2026 on a defined net basis. Annual operating losses can't stand in for quarterly net losses. The compound claim stays unsettled.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Firm language ('are toast', 'will make a beeline'), so it is scoreable in principle. The antecedent 'if VC dries up' is kept, and in context it governs both consequences.

contract.note: Defining 'dries up' as losing practical access to new funding and 'toast' as business failure is fair. No deadline is invented, and the separate runway remark is rightly left out.

evidence.note: SoftBank's own disclosure says its $30B follow-on investment was completed by Oct 1, 2026. That bears on the antecedent (funding has not dried up), not on the predicted consequences, so it is context rather than contradiction.
Reports executive departures in 2026, but not a funding cutoff and not moves to competitors. Isolated exits cannot resolve the forecast.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent has not happened: the evidence shows funding continuing, not a cutoff. The forecast has no deadline, so it can't be scored. Continued funding doesn't count as failure of the prediction, and no conclusive event has occurred.
